output.rationale: Start with a compact cause map, then use two teaching-and-recall cycles to build the outbreak sequence and the basic 1914 to 1918 timeline without overloading a novice.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions created a fragile balance of rival blocs and heightened crisis risk.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, then a chain of mobilization decisions and war declarations.
World War I runs from 1914 outbreak through 1918 armistice, so the main dates belong in one start-to-finish chronology.
completionEvidence: Name the main alliance blocs and at least one prewar tension.
Put Sarajevo, July Crisis, war declarations, 1914 outbreak, U.S. entry, and armistice in order.
Classify each uncertain item as a cause, event, or consequence.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a concise model, explain it in your own words, notice gaps, repair them, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the chain from causes to outbreak to chronology helps you build a usable big-picture map, not just isolated facts.
how: Explain the idea in plain language from memory.
Use the feedback to repair the missing piece.
Explain it again without copying the model.
methodBriefing.completion: You complete the session by attempting every required activity, including the repair and the final explanation.
personalization: Use one concrete example before the abstract map.
Keep only one action visible at a time.

activities.label: Model
activities.title: Why Europe Was So Tense
activities.body: Read the model and get the big picture first. Then you will explain it in your own words.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions created a fragile balance of rival blocs and heightened crisis risk.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: Tell the Outbreak Story
activities.body: Explain the sequence in your own words. Keep it short and concrete.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination in Sarajevo set off the July Crisis, and then mobilization decisions and war declarations turned the crisis into war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links Sarajevo to the July Crisis and then to mobilization and declarations of war. If it is incomplete, add the step that turns a political crisis into a wider war.

activities.label: Repair
activities.title: Fix the Missing Link
activities.body: Use the hint to repair your explanation. Then answer again.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Treating the Sarajevo assassination as the war itself instead of the trigger for the July Crisis and later declarations of war.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination was the trigger, not the whole war; the July Crisis and then mobilization and war declarations widened it into a larger conflict.
activities.feedback: The key correction is trigger versus full outbreak. The assassination started the crisis chain, and the war came after the July Crisis and declarations of war.

activities.label: Reexplain
activities.title: Map the First World War Years
activities.body: Explain the timeline from start to finish without looking at the model.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I begins in 1914, the United States enters in 1917, and the war ends with the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer puts the main dates in order and keeps 1914, 1917, and 1918 distinct. If needed, add that 1914 is the outbreak and 1918 is the armistice.

activities.label: Check
activities.title: Recognize the Timeline
activities.body: Choose the best timeline summary. Then check your answer.
choices: Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, war began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice came in 1918.
The armistice came first, then the war began, then Sarajevo happened, then the United States entered.
The United States entered before the war began, and the armistice came in 1914.
Sarajevo happened after the armistice, and the war began in 1918.
activities.correctAnswer: Sarajevo triggered the July Crisis, war began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice came in 1918.
activities.feedback: The correct timeline keeps the trigger, outbreak, U.S. entry, and armistice in order. Watch for answers that swap the years or treat Sarajevo as the war itself.

activities.label: Reflect
activities.title: Name the Three Pieces
activities.body: Write one sentence for each: cause, outbreak, and chronology. End with the one part you still want to review.

World War I runs from 1914 outbreak through 1918 armistice, so the main dates belong in one start-to-finish chronology.

items.essentialIdea: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into armed blocs before 1914.

check.title: Alliances before 1914
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
check.referenceAnswer: They divided Europe into armed alliance blocs, so a local crisis could pull multiple powers into war.
check.feedback: Correct: alliances made escalation more likely by linking separate states together.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered a diplomatic crisis that led to declarations of war.

check.title: From assassination to war
check.prompt: What chain of events connected the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war?
check.referenceAnswer: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo triggered an ultimatum, mobilizations, and then declarations of war.
check.feedback: Correct: the assassination set off the crisis sequence rather than causing all the fighting at once.

items.essentialIdea: Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 places World War I from outbreak to armistice.

check.title: War years in order
check.prompt: What is the basic chronology for World War I from 1914 to 1918?
check.referenceAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended with the armistice in 1918.
check.feedback: Correct: 1914 marks the outbreak and 1918 marks the war's end.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the war timeline
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which choice correctly states the basic World War I chronology?
choices: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
World War I began in 1918 and ended in 1914.
Prewar alliances formed after the war began.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Correct: those are the opening and closing years of the war.
